about: The named faults of geom-solidcore's tests at the pinned commit of solidcore (decision 32.70): each a test that fails by design, with the one cause of its failure. An SC entry is solidcore's fault: a case of tests/cases.json it answers wrongly. An entry marked ours is not solidcore's: a CK entry is a test the kernel's own checker (geom-check) lacks, a WR entry a limit of geom-solidcore's own interface or of its case table, each a kernel piece to open. Every test still expects the kernel's answer and fails; kernel.yml's jobs solidcore and solidcore-wasm pass only when the tests that fail are exactly the ones listed here. A fault of solidcore is fixed on the fork's branch, or the operation it blocks stays the kernel's own. An SC entry marked stays_ours is solidcore's fault for good: the operation it blocks stays the kernel's own, for the measured reason given. The upstream entry (SC-7) is solidcore's own suite at the pin: its tests and stored-answer units that need upstream test files the public repository does not hold, each named and counted, and each a named fault until it runs.

faults.fault: SC-1, two solids 1e-7 apart joined: solidcore's zone tolerance (1e-5) merges faces closer than it
faults.solidcore_gives: one solid of 6 faces and volume 2.0000001000000003
faults.expected: two lumps of 12 faces and volume 2, as the closed form and the kernel's exact geom-bool give
faults.blocks: flat-faced booleans: they stay on the kernel's exact geom-bool

faults.fault: WR-2 (ours: the case table, not solidcore), a length on no grid: the table writes the second wall's corner at 0.20000010000000001 m (the binary64 sum 0.2 + 1e-7, printed), and that decimal, read exactly, is not a whole number of steps of any grid, so the case is refused before solidcore is reached. Before lengths were read exactly it ran on Q1 as 32000016 steps and showed SC-3 (solidcore's zone tolerance of 1e-5 closes the 1e-7 gap: one solid of volume 4.20000006, 10 faces), which no case now reaches
faults.solidcore_gives: not reached: the test stops at "0.20000010000000001 m is not a whole number of steps of Q2"
faults.expected: two solids of 12 faces and volume 4.2, as the closed form gives
faults.blocks: nothing of solidcore's until the table writes the gap as a decimal on the grid (0.2000001); SC-3 still blocks the union of two solids whose faces come closer than 1e-5 without touching, which stays on the kernel's exact geom-bool

faults.fault: SC-4, a window leaving a sliver of 1e-6 above it loses the sliver: solidcore takes the cutter's top, 1e-6 below the wall's, as the wall's top
faults.solidcore_gives: volume 1.9999999999999993, one solid: the 1e-6 head over the window is gone
faults.expected: volume 2.0000002 (2.4 - 0.2 x 1 x (2 - 1e-6)), one solid with the sliver kept
faults.blocks: the difference of two solids (geom-solidcore's difference) where a face of the cutter comes within 1e-5 of a face of the body: openings in walls and slabs stay on the kernel's exact geom-bool

faults.fault: SC-5, a cylinder's cap off square to its axis: solidcore writes a cap of its cylinder on a plane about 2e-16 off square to the cylinder's axis (the cylinder of radius 0.5 and height 1 on the origin has its top cap's v axis (-1, 0, 2.1410351709324202e-16) and its origin at z = 0.9999999999999999), so the cap and the side do not meet in the one circle they share; group 3 of the kernel's checker certifies a plane and a cylinder meeting only along a shared full circle when the plane is exactly square to the axis, and so refuses the cylinder. The same rows with that one plane square pass (convert.rs, a_cylinder_fails_on_its_top_cap_alone)
faults.solidcore_gives: a cylinder the kernel's checker refuses, its first fault "group 3, face 0: no certified test of this pair exists yet (face 1)"
faults.expected: the case's answer in tests/cases.json, from a cylinder whose caps are square to its axis, as the kernel's geom-make writes its own
faults.blocks: every operation on a cylinder made by solidcore (geom-solidcore's cylinder, and the sections and booleans of one). Behind it (a diagnostic run with the caps written square, not committed), isect-21 to isect-27, isect-40, isect-41 and results_are_the_kernels_bodies pass, and the booleans of bool-22, bool-23, bool-24, bool-27, bldg-12, bldg-14, bldg-15, bldg-24, bldg-28 and bldg-29 meet unchecked pairs of group 3 (CK-2)
faults.stays_ours: stays ours for good (decision 32.76; the test the_kernel_makes_its_own_cylinder shows it): the kernel makes its own cylinder, and any body with a one-circle cap, exactly, with geom-make, and does not hand that operation to solidcore. Measured at the pin on 19 Nov 2026: solidcore's stored answers are the answers of its fitted cap normal's own rounding. With the cap written on the plane exactly square to the axis (the circle's frame's Z, or X cross Y of that frame, or the frame's Z only where it agrees with the fitted normal to rounding), the same 89 of solidcore's own stored answers change (boolean.api_brep 2, primitive.api_primitives 6, topology.api_files 64, topology.assert_valid 17), some by a lot (a body becomes failure 1001, a measure moves 2%): those cases sit on an edge the rounding decides, so no form of the fix leaves solidcore's stored answers as they are, and the pin does not move for it
